Standard: Store exhaust (e.g., gases, fluids, and particulates) and recoil forces do not obscure transparencies, damage structure or erode surfaces, ablate faces of flight-critical sensors, or degrade any other flight-critical systems (e.g., ECS, antenna, air data system). The air vehicle is capable of withstanding the impingement effects of store exhaust without weakening the skin of the air vehicle, degrading critical structure of the airframe, or degrading critical crew systems necessary for sustainment of flight. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examine store design documentation to determine the potential for store exhaust to impinge air vehicle surfaces and flight-critical systems.
(2) Verify the chemical composition, temperature, pressure and toxicity of any exhaust gases, fluids, or particulates to determine the impingement characteristics of the exhaust and plume. Analysis.
  (1) Conduct analysis to verify that store exhaust does not obscure transparencies, erode surfaces, ablate faces of sensors, or degrade other flight-critical systems.
  (2) Conduct analysis to verify the store exhaust gas and plume does not impinge on flight-critical sensors, target acquisition and designators (e.g., radar, laser) to ensure employment of stores does not result in degraded performance, unsafe conditions, or hazards.
  (3) Conduct analysis to verify the store exhaust, muzzle blast, overpressure, temperature, and recoil does not impinge or damage air vehicle structure, surfaces, or injure crewmembers. Test.
    (1) Ground test: Verify through static ground fire testing that gases and ejecta from gunfire and rocket motor operations do not obscure, ablate, erode or damage air vehicle surfaces or flight-critical sensors.
    (2) Flight test: Conduct live fire testing to measure store exhaust, muzzle and blast overpressure, temperature, and recoil forces to determine effects on transparencies, air vehicle surfaces and structure, flight-critical systems, and crew members IAW MIL-HDBK-1763, Test 160. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Demonstration.
      (1) Verify through ground or flight demonstration that stores can operate without obscuring transparencies, eroding surfaces, ablating faces of flight-critical sensors, or degrading other flight-critical systems or crew members.
